A pressure ulcer is defined as an area of localized damage to the skin and/or underlying tissue (usually over a bonyprominence)causedbypressure,orpressureincombinationwithshearstress.Pressureulcersdevelopwhen continuous pressure affects cellular metabolism and impedes or obstructs capillary blood flow to the skin and underlying tissue, resulting in tissue ischemia1 . Malnutrition is an independent risk factor for the development of pressure ulcers. Appropriate nutrition is imperative for preventing and treating such wounds. Reddy M et al.2 reviewed that protein supplementation of long-term care residents improved wound healing compared with a placebo(itbroughtaboutanimprovementinthePressureUlcerScaleforHealing[PUSH]score).Forundernourished patients, supplementation with high amounts of energy and protein is recommended. In addition, various vitamins, zinc, and arginine and collagen hydrolysates should be supplied3 . Collagen hydrolysate (CH), which is also referred to as collagen peptides, is widely utilized as a nutritional supplement. what_it_measured.text: The objective of the present study was to assess the clinical effectiveness of CH supplementation in terms of its ability to induce remission in subjects with stage II or III pressure ulcers and the safety of this approach.

This was a 16-week double-blind, multi-centric, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical study that aimed to determine the effectiveness, safety, and tolerability of CH (CH-a or CH-b) as an add-on nutritional supplement during the management of subjects with stage II or III pressure ulcers.

dose.text: The subjects were randomized to receive CH-a (n = 39), CH-b (n = 39), or a placebo (n = 42) twice daily (10 g per day) for 16 weeks.

route.text: The subjects were advised to orally consume 5 g of CH or the placebo, dissolved in 250 ml water or milk in the morning and night after eating food.

endpoint.text: The primary treatment efficacy endpoint was to compare CH group and placebo group for PUSH score, PSST score and wound area at week 16.

reported_results.text: Data are expressed as mean values (N = 38, 35, and 39 for the CH-a, CH-b and placebo groups, respectively).

numbers.text: The subjects were randomized to receive CH-a (n = 39), CH-b (n = 39), or a placebo (n = 42) twice daily (10 g per day) for 16 weeks.
The subjects were advised to orally consume 5 g of CH or the placebo, dissolved in 250 ml water or milk in the morning and night after eating food.
The primary treatment efficacy endpoint was to compare CH group and placebo group for PUSH score, PSST score and wound area at week 16.
Data are expressed as mean values (N = 38, 35, and 39 for the CH-a, CH-b and placebo groups, respectively).

This was a 16-week double-blind, multi-centric, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical study that aimed to determine the effectiveness, safety, and tolerability of CH (CH-a or CH-b) as an add-on nutritional supplement during the management of subjects with stage II or III pressure ulcers.
